text: This is Make Good: product recall refunds through PayPal, with proof behind every payment.

A supplier recalls one faulty batch. The shop must now find who received it. PayPal knows who paid, but not which batch anyone got, and the shop's records disagree: codes typed differently, missing batch numbers, two payments on one order. So shops refund everyone and lose money, or they wait, and customers open disputes.

Make Good asks two questions for every buyer. Is this their PayPal payment? Was their unit affected? Proven cases go on one exact list a person approves. Unclear ones are held, and the customer can be asked. Then PayPal refunds each customer once, before anyone needs a dispute.

caption: Open the recall demo
text: Here's the real app. Open the recall demo: thirty-two invented orders on a built-in PayPal simulator, and the labels say so on every screen.

caption: Find your way: the menu, the step tabs, Next step
text: The left menu is your workspace. Inside an incident, numbered tabs take you step by step, and Next step always says what to do.

caption: Step 1 · Read the supplier's notice
text: Step one reads the supplier's notice, with Gemini or with built-in rules. Every line quotes the notice, and nothing applies until a person saves it.

caption: Step 2 · Two questions for every buyer
text: Step two matches orders against PayPal. Orders can come from a spreadsheet. Each buyer gets two answers, crossed in this table. Green is ready, amber needs a person, and look-alike codes are decided by a person.

caption: Step 3 · The evidence behind every customer
text: Step three shows the evidence. Open a customer to see the facts. This order shipped while two batches were going out, so it's held, not paid.

caption: Ask the customer with a one-time link
text: When records can't settle it, email the customer a one-time link. They type the batch code, and staff still decide.

caption: Step 4 · Three refund policies, priced
text: Step four prices three refund policies, and shows who a looser rule would pay by mistake.

caption: Step 5 · Approve one exact payment list
text: Step five builds one exact payment list with a fingerprint. Any change after approval withdraws it.

caption: Step 6 · Pay through PayPal, even when a reply is lost
text: Step six pays through PayPal. Here we make PayPal lose a reply. That payment shows as unknown, not failed, and Make Good asks again with the same request ID. Nobody is paid twice.

caption: Customers told once, after PayPal confirms
text: Customers are emailed only after PayPal confirms, and every action lands on an audit trail.

caption: Claims, connections, team roles and monitoring
text: Around each recall: a claims page for customers the records missed, connections for PayPal, Shopify and WooCommerce, team roles for approvals, and monitoring.
It's built with Next.js and React, a Node and TypeScript API on PostgreSQL, PayPal's REST APIs, and Google Gemini, which only proposes and never pays.

To check it: every screen labels what's simulated, the run on PayPal's real sandbox lists PayPal's own refund IDs, and over a hundred and fifty tests run with one command. Try the live demo, upload your own orders, or make PayPal lose a reply.
Make Good. The right customers, refunded once, with proof.
